T: You're a wizard, Harry. You're also hungry.
D: An orphaned boy learns he's a wizard and starts his first year at a school of magic.
P: Serve the feast when the plates fill up at the welcome feast in the Great Hall.
S: the sweets trolley on the train to school

Milk chocolate frogs moulded around crunchy homemade honeycomb, each wrapped in a little paper card like the ones from the trolley. Line a tray with baking paper. Boil 150g caster sugar and 3 tbsp golden syrup to 150C, then whisk in 2 tsp bicarb, pour onto the tray and leave to set for 30 minutes. Break into small crumbs. Melt 250g milk chocolate gently. Spoon a little into frog moulds, add a pinch of honeycomb, top with more chocolate and tap out the air. Chill 30 minutes, turn out and wrap each in paper.
the rock-hard cakes at Hagrid's hut, softer here
Flour, butter, sugar, mixed fruit and spice rubbed together, bound with egg and milk, dropped in rough piles, baked at 200C for 15 minutes until golden but tender.
Roast pumpkin mashed with feta, sage and nutmeg, wrapped in shortcrust half moons, egg washed, baked at 200C for 20 minutes.
M: Roast chicken drumsticks glazed with honey and mustard, roast potatoes, Yorkshire puddings, buttered peas and carrots and gravy, all piled on the table at once.
the first proper Christmas Harry ever has

Herb-buttered turkey breast roasted golden with chipolatas in bacon, roast potatoes, honey parsnips, cranberry sauce and a rich gravy. Heat the oven to 180C. Rub a 1.5kg turkey breast roll with 50g butter mashed with sage and thyme and roast 75 minutes to 70C inside, then rest. Wrap 12 chipolatas in half rashers of streaky bacon and roast for the last 30 minutes. Roast 1kg parboiled potatoes and 500g parsnips tossed in honey and oil at 200C for 45 minutes. Make gravy with the tray juices, 1 tbsp flour and 400ml chicken stock. Serve with cranberry sauce.
W: Sweet shortcrust blind baked, filled with golden syrup warmed with fresh breadcrumbs, lemon zest and juice, baked at 180C for 30 minutes until set. Clotted cream.
K: the jug on every table in the Great Hall
Roast pumpkin blended with apple juice, a little honey and cinnamon, strained and served cold.

s.note: the rock-hard cakes at Hagrid's hut, softer here
s.how: Rub 125g butter into 250g self-raising flour with 75g sugar and a teaspoon of mixed spice. Stir in 150g mixed dried fruit, then bind with an egg and a splash of milk. Drop in rough piles on a tray and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden.

Roast 600g diced pumpkin at 200C until soft, then mash with 100g crumbled feta, chopped sage and a grating of nutmeg. Cut 3 sheets of shortcrust into rounds, fill and fold into half moons. Crimp the edges, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 20 minutes.

m.how: Glaze 8 chicken drumsticks with honey and wholegrain mustard and roast at 200C for 40 minutes alongside 1kg potato chunks. Whisk flour, egg and milk into a batter and bake in hot oiled muffin tins for 20 minutes. Serve with buttered peas and gravy.

w.how: Blind bake a sweet shortcrust case. Warm 400g golden syrup with 100g fresh white breadcrumbs, the zest and juice of a lemon, and pour into the case. Bake at 180C for 30 minutes until just set. Cool slightly and serve each slice with a spoon of clotted cream.

d.note: the jug on every table in the Great Hall
d.how: Roast 300g pumpkin until soft and cool it completely. Blend with 1L cloudy apple juice, a spoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon until smooth. Strain through a sieve into a jug, chill well and pour into goblets for the Great Hall table.
